# Event Schedule

> Event Schedule is an open-source event calendar and ticketing platform. A performer, a venue or a curator gets one public page for every event, with free registration and RSVP, ticket sales with zero platform fees through their own Stripe or PayPal account, two-way calendar sync, newsletters to the people who follow them, and QR tickets scanned at the door. It runs hosted at eventschedule.com or selfhosted, and has a full REST API with an OpenAPI 3.0 spec.

Key facts:

- **Schedule types**: three. Talent (performers and artists), Venue (places that host events) and Curator (guides that collect events from many talents and venues).
- **Free plan**: unlimited events and schedules, unlimited free registration and RSVP, zero-price ticket types, QR ticket scanning at the door, two-way Google Calendar, Outlook and CalDAV sync, analytics, event graphics, an embeddable calendar and iCal feeds, recurring events, sub-schedules, one appointment type, email subscribers with automatic new-event digests, 10 newsletter emails a month (each recipient counts as one), and AI event parsing. One team member per schedule.
- **Pro plan**: selling tickets that carry a price, with every payment method (Stripe, PayPal, Payfast, Invoice Ninja, a payment link or cash) and full or partial refunds; promo codes, add-ons, passes, gift cards, the ticket waitlist and installment payments; the live check-in dashboard and sales export; the REST API and webhooks; more appointment types and paid bookings; custom fields, custom CSS, polls, feedback and carpools; the embeddable ticket widget; no Event Schedule branding; 100 newsletter emails a month.
- **Enterprise plan**: everything in Pro, plus custom domains, allocated (reserved) seating with a box office console, multiple team members, internal and unlisted events, AI flyer, style and description generation, agenda scanning, WhatsApp event creation, availability management, 1,000 newsletter emails a month and priority support.
- **Selfhosted**: every Pro and Enterprise feature is included on your own server.
- **Fees**: zero platform fees on ticket sales, on every plan. Only the payment processor's own fee applies.
- **Open source**: the whole codebase is public under the Attribution Assurance License.
- **Languages**: 12 supported languages, with automatic translation of event content.

## Product

- [Features](https://eventschedule.com/features): Every feature, grouped by what it does
- [Pricing](https://eventschedule.com/pricing): Free, Pro and Enterprise, and what each adds
- [Ticketing](https://eventschedule.com/features/ticketing): Ticket types, QR check-in and payment into your own account
- [Free registration and RSVP](https://eventschedule.com/features/registration): Free sign-ups with a capacity per date and a waitlist
- [Calendar sync](https://eventschedule.com/features/calendar-sync): Two-way sync with Google Calendar, Outlook and CalDAV
- [Newsletters](https://eventschedule.com/features/newsletters): Newsletters and automatic new-event digests for followers
- [Appointments](https://eventschedule.com/features/appointments): Bookable appointment types on a public booking page
- [Allocated seating](https://eventschedule.com/features/allocated-seating): Seating plans, a guest seat picker and a box office console
- [AI](https://eventschedule.com/features/ai): Event parsing from text and images, agenda scanning and translation
- [Embed calendar](https://eventschedule.com/features/embed-calendar): The live calendar on any website with one iframe tag
- [Integrations](https://eventschedule.com/features/integrations): Stripe, PayPal, Invoice Ninja, calendars and more

## Who it is for

- [Use cases](https://eventschedule.com/use-cases): Performers, venues, curators, communities and online events
- [For talent](https://eventschedule.com/for-talent): Musicians, DJs, comedians and every other kind of performer
- [For venues](https://eventschedule.com/for-venues): Bars, clubs, theaters, restaurants and every space that hosts events
- [For curators](https://eventschedule.com/for-curators): Local event guides that collect events from many sources

## API

- **Authentication**: API key via `X-API-Key` header, obtained through registration or login
- **Plans**: Most of the API is on the Pro plan: schedule, event, sub-schedule and sale endpoints return only Pro schedules' data, or a 403. Creating or deleting a schedule, the category list, fan content and recording a sale (`POST /api/sales`, free ticket tiers only unless the schedule is Pro) have no Pro check.
- **Rate limits**: 300 GET requests/min, 30 POST/PUT/DELETE requests/min, counted per IP address
- **Getting started**: register (`POST /api/register`; hosted mode requires email verification via `POST /api/register/send-code` first), create a schedule (`POST /api/schedules` with a name and type: venue, talent or curator), then create events (`POST /api/events/{subdomain}`)
- [llms-full.txt](https://eventschedule.com/llms-full.txt): Complete self-contained documentation for LLMs (no link-following needed)
- [API Reference](https://eventschedule.com/docs/developer/api): Full API documentation with examples for all endpoints
- [OpenAPI Spec](https://eventschedule.com/api/openapi.json): OpenAPI 3.0 specification for client generation and tool integration
- [agents.json](https://eventschedule.com/.well-known/agents.json): Agent workflow definitions for multi-step API tasks
- [For AI Agents](https://eventschedule.com/for-ai-agents): Overview of API capabilities for AI agents and developers
